passages.text: On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, the women came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared.
passages.sermon:
The women had come with Jesus from Galilee.
They followed Him.
On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, these women went to the tomb.
They brought the spices they had prepared.
passages.original: Τῇ δὲ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ὄρθρου βαθέως ἐπὶ τὸ μνῆμα ἦλθον φέρουσαι ἃ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα

passages.text: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb, but when they entered, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
passages.sermon:
The women went to the tomb of Jesus.
They saw the stone was rolled away from the entrance.
They entered the tomb.
They did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
passages.original: εὗρον δὲ τὸν λίθον ἀποκεκυλισμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου εἰσελθοῦσαι δὲ οὐχ εὗρον τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: While they were puzzling over this, suddenly two men in radiant apparel stood beside them.
passages.sermon:
The women stood at the tomb.
They did not find the body of Jesus.
They felt confused.
Suddenly, two men appeared beside them.
The two men wore shining clothes.
passages.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἀπορεῖσθαι αὐτὰς περὶ τούτου καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο ἐπέστησαν αὐταῖς ἐν ἐσθῆτι ἀστραπτούσῃ

passages.text: As the women bowed their faces to the ground in terror, the two men asked them, “Why do you look for the living among the dead?
passages.sermon:
Two men stood beside the women.
The men wore radiant clothing.
The women felt afraid.
The women bowed their faces to the ground.
The two men spoke to the women.
The men asked, “Why do you look for the living among the dead?”
passages.original: ἐμφόβων δὲ γενομένων αὐτῶν καὶ κλινουσῶν τὰ πρόσωπα εἰς τὴν γῆν εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτάς Τί ζητεῖτε τὸν ζῶντα μετὰ τῶν νεκρῶν

passages.text: He is not here; He has risen! Remember how He told you while He was still in Galilee: ‘The Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and on the third day rise again.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is not here.
Jesus has risen.
Remember what Jesus told you in Galilee.
Jesus said, “The Son of Man must be handed over to sinful men.
They will crucify Him.
On the third day, He will rise again.”
passages.original: οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε ἀλλὰ ἠγέρθη μνήσθητε ὡς ἐλάλησεν ὑμῖν ἔτι ὢν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ λέγων Τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὅτι δεῖ παραδοθῆναι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ σταυρωθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἀναστῆναι

passages.text: Then they remembered His words.
passages.sermon: The women remembered the words of Jesus.\r\nThey recalled what He had said before.\r\nThey understood His message.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐμνήσθησαν τῶν ῥημάτων αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And when they returned from the tomb, they reported all these things to the Eleven and to all the others.
passages.sermon:
The women left the tomb.
They went back to the others.
They told all these things to the Eleven disciples.
They also told everything to all the other followers.
passages.original: καὶ ὑποστρέψασαι ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου ἀπήγγειλαν ταῦτα πάντα τοῖς ἕνδεκα καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς λοιποῖς

passages.text: It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told this to the apostles.
passages.sermon:
Mary Magdalene was there.
Joanna was there.
Mary, the mother of James, was there.
Other women were with them.
These women spoke to the apostles.
They told the apostles these things.
passages.original: ἦσαν δὲ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ Μαρία καὶ Ἰωάννα καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰακώβου καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ σὺν αὐταῖς ἔλεγον πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ταῦτα

passages.text: But their words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.
passages.sermon: The apostles heard the women’s report.\r\nThe apostles thought the women’s words sounded like nonsense.\r\nThe apostles did not believe the women.
passages.original: καὶ ἐφάνησαν ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ λῆρος τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα καὶ ἠπίστουν αὐταῖς

passages.text: Peter, however, got up and ran to the tomb. And after bending down and seeing only the linen cloths, he went away, wondering to himself what had happened.
passages.sermon:
Peter was one of Jesus’ disciples.
Peter stood up.
Peter ran to the tomb.
Peter bent down at the tomb.
Peter saw only the linen cloths lying there.
Peter did not see Jesus’ body.
Peter left the tomb.
Peter wondered to himself about what had happened.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἀναστὰς ἔδραμεν ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ παρακύψας βλέπει τὰ ὀθόνια μόνα καὶ ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς αὑτὸν θαυμάζων τὸ γεγονός

passages.text: That same day two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Two of Jesus’ followers walked together that day.
They left Jerusalem.
They traveled to a village named Emmaus.
Emmaus was about seven miles from Jerusalem.
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἦσαν πορευόμενοι εἰς κώμην ἀπέχουσαν σταδίους ἑξήκοντα ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλήμ ᾗ ὄνομα Ἐμμαοῦς

passages.text: They were talking with each other about everything that had happened.
passages.sermon: Two of Jesus’ followers walked together to Emmaus.\r\nThey talked with each other.\r\nThey spoke about everything that had happened.
passages.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡμίλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους περὶ πάντων τῶν συμβεβηκότων τούτων

passages.text: And as they talked and deliberated, Jesus Himself came up and walked along with them.
passages.sermon:
Two of Jesus’ followers walked to Emmaus.
They talked with each other.
They discussed everything that had happened.
Jesus Himself came near them.
Jesus walked with them.
passages.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὁμιλεῖν αὐτοὺς καὶ συζητεῖν καὶ αὐτὸς Ἰησοῦς ἐγγίσας συνεπορεύετο αὐτοῖς

passages.text: But their eyes were kept from recognizing Him.
passages.sermon: The men walked with Jesus.\r\nThey did not know it was Jesus.\r\nSomething kept their eyes from seeing who He was.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν ἐκρατοῦντο τοῦ μὴ ἐπιγνῶναι αὐτόν

passages.text: He asked them, “What are you discussing so intently as you walk along?” They stood still, with sadness on their faces.
passages.sermon:
Jesus walked with the two disciples.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus asked a question.
He said, “What are you talking about as you walk together?”
The two disciples stopped walking.
They looked sad.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς Τίνες οἱ λόγοι οὗτοι οὓς ἀντιβάλλετε πρὸς ἀλλήλους περιπατοῦντες Καὶ ἐστάθησαν σκυθρωποί

passages.text: One of them, named Cleopas, asked Him, “Are You the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in recent days?”
passages.sermon:
One of the men was named Cleopas.
Cleopas spoke to Jesus.
He asked Jesus a question.
He said, “Are you the only visitor in Jerusalem?”
He asked if Jesus did not know what had happened there in these recent days.
passages.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἷς ὀνόματι Κλεοπᾶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν Σὺ μόνος παροικεῖς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ οὐκ ἔγνως τὰ γενόμενα ἐν αὐτῇ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις

passages.text: “What things?” He asked. “The events involving Jesus of Nazareth,” they answered. “This man was a prophet, powerful in speech and action before God and all the people.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to two disciples walking to Emmaus.
He asked them, “What things?”
The disciples answered Him.
They spoke about Jesus of Nazareth.
Jesus of Nazareth was a man.
He was a prophet.
He was powerful in what He did.
He was powerful in what He said.
He was powerful before God.
He was powerful before all the people.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ποῖα οἱ Δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Τὰ περὶ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζαρηνοῦ ὃς ἐγένετο ἀνὴρ προφήτης δυνατὸς ἐν ἔργῳ καὶ λόγῳ ἐναντίον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ

passages.text: Our chief priests and rulers delivered Him up to the sentence of death, and they crucified Him.
passages.sermon:
Our chief priests handed Jesus over.
Our rulers also handed Jesus over.
They gave Him to be judged.
They sentenced Him to death.
They crucified Him.
passages.original: ὅπως τε παρέδωκαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες ἡμῶν εἰς κρίμα θανάτου καὶ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτόν

passages.text: But we were hoping He was the One who would redeem Israel. And besides all this, it is the third day since these things took place.
passages.sermon: We hoped Jesus would redeem Israel.\r\nHe is the one we expected to save our people.\r\nBut now, three days have passed since these things happened.
passages.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἠλπίζομεν ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ μέλλων λυτροῦσθαι τὸν Ἰσραήλ ἀλλά γε καὶ σὺν πᾶσιν τούτοις τρίτην ταύτην ἡμέραν ἄγει ἀφ’ οὗ ταῦτα ἐγένετο

passages.text: Furthermore, some of our women astounded us. They were at the tomb early this morning, but they did not find His body. They came and told us they had seen a vision of angels, who said that Jesus was alive.
passages.sermon:
Some women from our group amazed us.
They went to the tomb early this morning.
They did not find Jesus’ body.
They returned and told us what happened.
They said they saw a vision of angels.
The angels said that Jesus is alive.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ καὶ γυναῖκές τινες ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξέστησαν ἡμᾶς γενόμεναι ὀρθριναὶ ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ μὴ εὑροῦσαι τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ ἦλθον λέγουσαι καὶ ὀπτασίαν ἀγγέλων ἑωρακέναι οἳ λέγουσιν αὐτὸν ζῆν

passages.text: Then some of our companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had described. But Him they did not see.”
passages.sermon: Some of our companions went to the tomb.\r\nThey found the tomb just as the women had described.\r\nThey did not see Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ ἀπῆλθόν τινες τῶν σὺν ἡμῖν ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ εὗρον οὕτως καθὼς καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες εἶπον αὐτὸν δὲ οὐκ εἶδον

passages.text: Then Jesus said to them, “O foolish ones, how slow are your hearts to believe all that the prophets have spoken!
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
He addressed the people walking with Him.
He called them foolish.
He said their hearts were slow to believe.
He referred to everything the prophets had spoken.
He said they did not believe all the prophets’ words.
passages.original: Καὶ αὐτὸς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ὦ ἀνόητοι καὶ βραδεῖς τῇ καρδίᾳ τοῦ πιστεύειν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἐλάλησαν οἱ προφῆται

passages.text: Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and then to enter His glory?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the two disciples.
Jesus called them foolish and slow to believe.
Jesus referred to the Christ.
The Christ is God’s chosen one.
The Christ had to suffer these things.
The Christ had to enter His glory after suffering.
It was necessary for the Christ to suffer.
It was necessary for the Christ to enter His glory.
passages.original: οὐχὶ ταῦτα ἔδει παθεῖν τὸν Χριστὸν καὶ εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the two disciples.
He began with the writings of Moses.
He also used the words of all the Prophets.
He explained to them what the Scriptures said about Himself.
He showed them these things in every part of the Scriptures.
passages.original: καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ Μωϋσέως καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν προφητῶν διερμήνευσεν αὐτοῖς ἐν πάσαις ταῖς γραφαῖς τὰ περὶ ἑαυτοῦ

passages.text: As they approached the village where they were headed, He seemed to be going farther.
passages.sermon:
Jesus walked with two disciples after His resurrection.
They all traveled toward a village.
They came near the village where they were going.
Jesus acted as if He would continue traveling farther.
passages.original: Καὶ ἤγγισαν εἰς τὴν κώμην οὗ ἐπορεύοντο καὶ αὐτὸς προσεποιήσατο πορρώτερον πορεύεσθαι

passages.text: But they pleaded with Him, “Stay with us, for it is nearly evening and the day is almost over.” So He went in to stay with them.
passages.sermon:
Two disciples walked with Jesus.
They did not recognize Him at first.
They reached the village where they were going.
Jesus seemed ready to continue on His way.
The disciples pleaded with Jesus.
They said, “Stay with us.”
They explained, “It is nearly evening.”
They said, “The day is almost over.”
Jesus agreed to stay with them.
He went in to stay with them.
passages.original: καὶ παρεβιάσαντο αὐτὸν λέγοντες Μεῖνον μεθ’ ἡμῶν ὅτι πρὸς ἑσπέραν ἐστὶν καὶ κέκλικεν ἤδη ἡ ἡμέρα Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν τοῦ μεῖναι σὺν αὐτοῖς

passages.text: While He was reclining at the table with them, He took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was sitting at the table with them.
He took bread.
He spoke a blessing over the bread.
He broke the bread.
He gave the bread to them.
passages.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ κατακλιθῆναι αὐτὸν μετ’ αὐτῶν λαβὼν τὸν ἄρτον εὐλόγησεν καὶ κλάσας ἐπεδίδου αὐτοῖς

passages.text: Then their eyes were opened and they recognized Jesus—and He disappeared from their sight.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sat at the table with two disciples.
The disciples did not recognize Jesus at first.
Suddenly, God opened the eyes of the disciples.
The disciples saw and recognized Jesus.
Jesus immediately disappeared from their sight.
passages.original: αὐτῶν δὲ διηνοίχθησαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτόν καὶ αὐτὸς ἄφαντος ἐγένετο ἀπ’ αὐτῶν

passages.text: They asked each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”
passages.sermon:
Two disciples of Jesus spoke to each other.
They remembered their experience with Jesus on the road.
They said, “Our hearts were burning within us.”
This happened while Jesus talked with them on the road.
Jesus explained the Scriptures to them during that time.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς ἀλλήλους Οὐχὶ ἡ καρδία ἡμῶν καιομένη ἦν ἐν ἡμῖν ὡς ἐλάλει ἡμῖν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ὡς διήνοιγεν ἡμῖν τὰς γραφάς

passages.text: And they got up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem. There they found the Eleven and those with them, gathered together and saying, “The Lord has indeed risen and has appeared to Simon!”
passages.sermon:
Two disciples recognized Jesus after He broke bread with them.
They immediately got up.
They returned to Jerusalem at that very hour.
They found the Eleven apostles gathered together.
Others were with the Eleven.
The group was saying, “The Lord has indeed risen.”
They said, “He has appeared to Simon.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀναστάντες αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ καὶ εὗρον ἠθροισμένους τοὺς ἕνδεκα καὶ τοὺς σὺν αὐτοῖς λέγοντας ὅτι Ὄντως ἠγέρθη ὁ Κύριος καὶ ὤφθη Σίμωνι

passages.text: Then the two told what had happened on the road, and how they had recognized Jesus in the breaking of the bread.
passages.sermon:
Two disciples spoke to the others.
They explained what happened to them on the road.
They told how they recognized Jesus.
They recognized Him when He broke the bread.
passages.original: Καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐξηγοῦντο τὰ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ καὶ ὡς ἐγνώσθη αὐτοῖς ἐν τῇ κλάσει τοῦ ἄρτου

passages.text: While they were describing these events, Jesus Himself stood among them and said, “Peace be with you.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the risen Lord.
The disciples were talking about what happened.
Jesus Himself stood among them.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus said, “Peace be with you.”
passages.original: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτῶν λαλούντων αὐτὸς ἔστη ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν

passages.text: But they were startled and frightened, thinking they had seen a spirit.
passages.sermon:
The disciples saw Jesus suddenly appear among them.
They felt startled.
They became afraid.
They thought they saw a spirit.
passages.original: πτοηθέντες δὲ καὶ ἔμφοβοι γενόμενοι ἐδόκουν πνεῦμα θεωρεῖν

passages.text: “Why are you troubled,” Jesus asked, “and why do doubts arise in your hearts?
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood among His disciples.
Jesus saw that His disciples felt troubled.
Jesus saw that His disciples had doubts in their hearts.
Jesus asked them a question.
Jesus said, “Why are you troubled?”
Jesus said, “Why do doubts arise in your hearts?”
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τί τεταραγμένοι ἐστέ καὶ διὰ τί διαλογισμοὶ ἀναβαίνουσιν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμῶν

passages.text: Look at My hands and My feet. It is I Myself. Touch Me and see—for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Look at My hands.
Look at My feet.
You see that it is really Me.
Touch Me and see for yourselves.
A spirit does not have flesh and bones.
You see that I have flesh and bones.”
passages.original: ἴδετε τὰς χεῖράς μου καὶ τοὺς πόδας μου ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι αὐτός ψηλαφήσατέ με καὶ ἴδετε ὅτι πνεῦμα σάρκα καὶ ὀστέα οὐκ ἔχει καθὼς ἐμὲ θεωρεῖτε ἔχοντα

passages.text: And when He had said this, He showed them His hands and feet.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He finished speaking.
He showed His hands to them.
He showed His feet to them.
passages.original: καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἔδειξεν αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τοὺς πόδας

passages.text: While they were still in disbelief because of their joy and amazement, He asked them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before His disciples.
The disciples felt great joy.
They also felt amazement.
They could not believe what they saw.
Jesus spoke to them.
He asked, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
passages.original: Ἔτι δὲ ἀπιστούντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς καὶ θαυμαζόντων εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἔχετέ τι βρώσιμον ἐνθάδε

passages.text: So they gave Him a piece of broiled fish, and He took it and ate it in front of them.
passages.sermon: The disciples gave Jesus a piece of broiled fish.\r\nJesus took the fish.\r\nJesus ate the fish in front of the disciples.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἐπέδωκαν αὐτῷ ἰχθύος ὀπτοῦ μέρος καὶ λαβὼν ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ἔφαγεν

passages.text: Jesus said to them, “These are the words I spoke to you while I was still with you: Everything must be fulfilled that is written about Me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “These are My words.
I spoke these words to you before.
I was still with you then.
Everything written about Me must happen.
These things are written in the Law of Moses.
They are also written in the Prophets.
They are also written in the Psalms.
All these writings speak about Me.
All these things must be fulfilled.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς Οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι μου οὓς ἐλάλησα πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἔτι ὢν σὺν ὑμῖν ὅτι δεῖ πληρωθῆναι πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα ἐν τῷ νόμῳ Μωϋσέως καὶ τοῖς προφήταις καὶ ψαλμοῖς περὶ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: Then He opened their minds to understand the Scriptures.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His disciples.
Jesus acted with power and authority.
Jesus opened the minds of His disciples.
He enabled them to understand the Scriptures.
passages.original: τότε διήνοιξεν αὐτῶν τὸν νοῦν τοῦ συνιέναι τὰς γραφάς

passages.text: And He told them, “This is what is written: The Christ will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day, and in His name repentance and forgiveness of sins will be proclaimed to all nations, beginning in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, "This is written in the Scriptures."
The Scriptures say the Christ must suffer.
The Scriptures say the Christ will rise from the dead on the third day.
In the name of Christ, people will preach repentance.
In the name of Christ, people will preach forgiveness of sins.
People will preach these things to all nations.
They will begin preaching in Jerusalem.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὕτως γέγραπται παθεῖν τὸν Χριστὸν καὶ ἀναστῆναι ἐκ νεκρῶν τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ κηρυχθῆναι ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ μετάνοιαν εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἀρξάμενοι ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλήμ

passages.text: You are witnesses of these things.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, "You are witnesses."
You have seen these things.
You know what happened.
You can tell others about these things.
passages.original: ὑμεῖς ἐστε μάρτυρες τούτων

passages.text: And behold, I am sending the promise of My Father upon you. But remain in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “I am sending you what my Father promised.
This promise comes from God the Father.
You must stay in the city.
Stay there until you receive power from above.
This power will come to you from heaven.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐξαποστέλλω τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ Πατρός μου ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ὑμεῖς δὲ καθίσατε ἐν τῇ πόλει ἕως οὗ ἐνδύσησθε ἐξ ὕψους δύναμιν

passages.text: When Jesus had led them out as far as Bethany, He lifted up His hands and blessed them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the subject.
Jesus led His disciples.
He took them outside the city.
He brought them as far as Bethany.
Jesus lifted up His hands.
He blessed His disciples.
passages.original: Ἐξήγαγεν δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔξω ἕως πρὸς Βηθανίαν καὶ ἐπάρας τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ εὐλόγησεν αὐτούς

passages.text: While He was blessing them, He left them and was carried up into heaven.
passages.sermon: Jesus was blessing His disciples.\r\nHe left them.\r\nHe was carried up into heaven.
passages.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εὐλογεῖν αὐτὸν αὐτοὺς διέστη ἀπ’ αὐτῶν καὶ ἀνεφέρετο εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν

passages.text: And they worshiped Him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy, praising God continually in the temple.
passages.sermon:
The disciples worshiped Jesus.
They returned to Jerusalem.
They felt great joy.
They stayed in the temple.
They praised God continually.
passages.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ προσκυνήσαντες αὐτὸν ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ μετὰ χαρᾶς μεγάλης καὶ ἦσαν διὰ παντὸς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ εὐλογοῦντες τὸν Θεόν
